title: feat(ui): original SVG operation icons and the SVG-to-PNG icon pipeline
body:
Slice 1 of #661: the SVG-to-PNG icon pipeline and the operation icons (checklist sections 1-3). Every `OpType` now has its own icon.

## What changed
- **Pipeline (`cargo xtask icons`, new `xtask/src/icons.rs`).** Each icon has an SVG master in `assets/ui/svg/*.svg`. The command rasterises it to the 32x32 PNG the UI already embeds (`assets/ui/<stem>.png`), and the PNGs are committed. `--check` re-renders every master and fails when a committed PNG differs from it (more than 8 per channel) or when a master breaks the house rules. `--sheet <out.png> [--px 16] [--zoom 4]` draws a contact sheet on a dark band and a light band so a person can look at the set. Rendering uses `resvg =0.45.1` (MIT OR Apache-2.0) with default features off. It is an **xtask-only** dependency: nothing new at runtime in the app or ui crates, and no `build.rs`. It reuses the lock's existing `tiny-skia 0.11`.
- **House rules (enforced by the lint):** Tabler conventions (`viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, no intrinsic size, round caps and joins, stroke 2 for the object and 1.5 for a toolpath/detail line), `currentColor` ink, shapes only (no image, script, text, style, href, `url(` or font). The loader still sets every pixel to white and lets alpha draw, so one PNG works in both themes.
- **41 original operation icons** (22 new, 5 stand-ins redrawn, 13 earlier originals redrawn, plus Trochoidal Slot and Plasma Profile, which are in the enum now). Each is drawn from what the operation does: a cutter and its path. Each family shares a frame: 2D in plan or section; multi-axis on a dome with the ball leaning on its normal; rotary on a bar with the tool riding the radial; every turning kind with a solid chuck block on the left.
- **Wiring.** `icons.rs` is now one macro table that generates the enum, `ALL`, the bytes and the texture keys (195 lines). `op_icon` moved out of the oversized `panes.rs` into a new `op_icons.rs` and maps every kind to its own slot; the old reuse law is retired. The turning section door now uses the Facing icon. Face is drawn in plan view, Facing in side view. The 18 PNGs nothing uses any more (13 earlier originals and 5 Tabler stand-ins) are deleted. `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` is updated: the op icons and their masters are ours, and the Tabler list excludes them.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` -> 24 (main reads 23 after #1100) (`xtask/` is a process file). Fork note for #681: no action beyond the normal process sync; the new `icons` task needs `resvg` in the lock, which the synced `xtask/Cargo.toml` brings in.

## Icons by source
| Drawn original | Tabler |
|---|---|
| all 41 `op-*` icons (face, contour, pocket, adaptive2d, offset2d, slot, trochoidal-slot, trace, engrave, chamfer2d, deburr, circular, plasma-profile, drill, bore, thread, probe, pocket3d, finish3d, contour5d, parallel5d, swarf, advanced-swarf, rotary-contour, rotary-parallel, rotary-offset, multiaxis-rough, flow5d, multiaxis-contour, facing, profile-rough, profile-finish, groove-rough, groove-finish, part-off, threading, chamfering, taper-turning, multipass-turning, form-turning, boring-turning) | none new (the chrome icons are unchanged) |

Nothing comes from HSMWorks, Fusion or SolidCraft. SolidCraft's interface material has been under its own brand licence since upstream 312454f899 (recorded in the decision).

## Merged main (2026-11-12, about 55 merges)
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`: conflict; now 24.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs`: conflict. Kept main's new `ribbon_labels_whole_and_captions_painted` (#948). Main's version brings the file to 398 lines, so my `every_op_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon` moved, unchanged, into a new `tests/op_icon_table.rs`.
- `Cargo.lock`, `xtask/` (#965/#967 gate rework), `panes.rs`, `icons.rs`, `mod.rs`: merged without conflicts. `Cargo.lock` adds only `resvg` and its dependencies; existing entries changed only by gaining version suffixes (`png 0.18.1`, `kurbo 0.13.1`, `base64 0.13.1`), with no version moved. `OpType` on main has the same 41 kinds, so nothing new needed carrying into `op_icons.rs`.

## Decision
`docs/decisions/661-icon-set.md` covers the pipeline, the dependency, the house rules, the SolidCraft licence finding, and what was considered and dropped.

## How tested (pinning tests)
- xtask: `committed_icon_pngs_match_their_svg_masters` (every committed PNG matches a fresh render of its master), `lint_accepts_a_clean_master`, `lint_refuses_raster_scripts_text_and_external_refs`, `lint_refuses_off_grid_sizes_caps_and_weights`, `render_draws_ink_on_the_32_px_grid`. `cargo test -p xtask`: 38 passed.
- ui structural (`tests/op_icon_table.rs`): `every_op_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon` checks that every `KindInfo::ALL` kind maps to its own `op-*` icon with an SVG master, and that no two slots share a PNG.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui` (all suites, CWD `crates/ui`): green, lib 532 passed. `cargo clippy -p xtask -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean. `cargo xtask icons --check`: 0 breaches.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` falls back to **batch** because of the `Cargo.lock` change. The batch steps I did not run are the geometry/cl/tools/post/sim/motion/app suites. Their crates are untouched, and `resvg` only enters xtask's graph.
- Looked at: every icon at 32 px and the whole set at 16 px on dark and light (`cargo xtask icons --sheet sheet.png --px 16 --zoom 4`, and `--px 32 --zoom 2`).

## Least happy with
- **Thread milling**: the sawtooth hole walls are busy at 16 px.
- **Advanced Swarf**: a curved blade with the tool at two poses reads as "two tools" more than as "swarf, advanced".
- (Redrawn after review: Face is now a plan view with a serpentine raster, so it no longer echoes Facing; Groove Rough is the plunge comb with the blade lifted and Groove Finish the bare U finishing path, which now read apart at 16 px.)
- **5-axis Contour**: the ring arcs crowd the dome at 16 px.
- **Deburr**: a small ball on a broken corner; it is the subtlest icon in the set.

## Not exercised
Not seen in the running app (no GUI launch): the toolbar, tree rows and operation pages with the new textures.

## Snapshots
No file under `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/` is changed. The toolbar and tree icons will render differently in the release-lane pixel goldens (`egui_app*.png`), so those need the normal refresh at the next cut.

## Still owed on #661
Section 4 (tool types), 6 (tree rows), 7 (status badges), 8 (actions); section 5 (tabs) lands with #659.

Effort: high (not escalated)

Changelog: Every operation kind has its own original icon in the toolbar and the tree (turning, holes, 3D, multi-axis, 2D); icons are now SVG masters rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`. (#661)

Refs #661

title: feat(app): work offsets post as an index bounded by the setup's own post (#931 slice 2)
body:
## What changed (slice 2 of 3: app)

Stacked on #1101 (slice 1), which stacks on #945. Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

The app now hands the post the setup's 1-based work-offset index, not a word. The setup's own post sets the limit; core keeps only a sanity bound.

- **The stream carries the index.** `camcraft_post::post::Dump::wcs` is now a `u32`, where 1 is the first offset. `posting::wcs_context` returns `(index, origin)`. The post writes the word.
- **No fallback (triage point 2).** `setup::work_offset` no longer filters the stored pick. If a setup's post cannot express the stored offset, the offset is still never read as offset 1 or G54. That holds for the stream, the travel check, the label and the setup sheet.
- **Post-time gate.** New `setup_offsets::range_problems`, part of `verification_report`, so it applies to the single-file, per-mount and per-op posts. It checks each setup that has an operation against that setup's own post (`setup_mount::post_of`). An offset the post cannot express blocks the post, naming the setup and the post. Slice 1's engine refusal still runs behind it.
- **Command-time check.** `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` checks the pick against the setup's post (`setup_offsets::check`) and refuses by name.
- **Loader.** The six-offset cap is removed from `project/apply.rs`. Only the sanity bound remains (pick 0..=254, the `u8` that the height digest stores).
- **Names.** New `setup::work_offset_names(world, setup)` reads slice 1's `work_offsets(cps)` table. It is cached per (resolved post, script text) in a bounded map. `setup::offset_name`, `setup::wcs_name` and `setup::wcs_label` use it, and so do the setup sheet, the refusal texts, the spindle-law text and the shared-offset clause. The names are for display only and never go into the stream.
- **File format.** Offsets 1-6 are still saved as `G54`..`G59`, so existing files round-trip byte-identical. Offsets 7 and up are saved as their number. **Builds older than this one cannot open a file that uses offset 7 or higher.** The decision file records this for the release notes (point 8).
- **`WCS_SLOTS` is split (point 1).** It is now a crate-private `LEGACY_WCS_NAMES`, used only for legacy entity-name reservations and the pre-v52 and pre-v54 migrations. All of its word uses are gone.
- **`shared_word_problems` (point 7)** compares offset indexes and names the offset by the post's name.
- **UI and MCP** keep working through the app functions. The Setups combo still lists offsets 1-6, now named by the setup's post. MCP still accepts the words G54-G59. Slice 3 changes the combo and adds MCP's `index`.

## How tested

- Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/wcs_index.rs`:
  - `offset_nine_on_a_six_offset_post_refuses_by_setup_name_and_never_posts_at_offset_one` (the no-fallback pin)
  - `the_command_refuses_an_offset_the_setups_post_cannot_express`
  - `the_setups_post_names_its_offsets`
  - `offset_seven_and_up_saves_as_its_number_and_reloads`
- Unit test: `project::wcs_pick::tests::legacy_words_and_numbers_round_trip`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 671ccd19: post suites, about 250 app suites including `wcs_index`, `setup_wcs`, `posting`, `probe_*`, `project_roundtrip` and `conformance`, the ui lib plus 11 ui suites. Wall time 9.6 min.
- I also ran 23 golden and post suites that the quick gate does not pick, including `golden_cl`, `carvera_post`, `heidenhain_*`, `tormach_post` and `lathe_post_*`. All pass, and no golden file changed.

title: feat(post): work offsets ride the stream as a 1-based index; the post writes the word
body:
Slice 1 of 3 for #931: the post crate and scripts. Stacked on #945 (#934, Sinumerik G505/G506). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

**This changes the post interface** (what every script receives as `PARAM WorkOffset`), so it waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.

## What changed

- **The stream carries the index.** `dump` writes `PARAM WorkOffset` as the setup's 1-based offset number (`G55` -> `2`). App still hands the word and still caps at 6; slice 2 makes the `Dump` field an index.
- **New `workOffsetIndex` manifest flag** (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs`, on the `coolantModes` pattern). It is read once at load with `workOffsetMax` (6 when unstated):
  - A flagged script receives the number. The engine refuses an offset above its maximum by setup name.
  - An unflagged (user) script receives the word `G54`..`G59` for 1-6, exactly as before. Any offset above 6 is refused by setup name, and an unflagged script cannot raise its own maximum.
  - The legacy words `G54`..`G59` in a stream still read as 1-6. Any other value (`G53`, 0, 2.5, `G54.1 P3`) is refused by setup name before a script sees it.
  - `work_offset::work_offsets(cps)` returns the maximum and the `workOffsetName(n)` names for slice 2's display. It never feeds the stream.
- **All 11 shipped scripts** declare the flag, `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName`, and map the index to their own word. No `slotOf` / `frameWord` / `frameOf` word parsing remains:
  - The Fanuc-family probe register reads `wcsIndex - 1`.
  - Sinumerik's `$P_UIFR[n]` uses the number directly.
  - Heidenhain maps offset n to preset row n.
- **Declared maxima:**
  - Tormach mill and Tormach lathe: **9** (`G59.1`..`G59.3`, cited to the LinuxCNC G-code reference: "G54-G59.3 Select Coordinate System (1 - 9)" and its G10 L2 table).
  - Every other dialect: **6**. Haas G154, Fanuc/Mazak/Doosan G54.1 P and further Sinumerik/Heidenhain frames or rows were not verified against a public manual, so none is written. Reasons and sources are in `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-post.md`.
- **Docs.** `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents the 1-based `WorkOffset` beside the probe's 0-based `SetWorkOffset` (triage point 4). `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describes the flag, the maximum and the name function.

## Tests

- New `crates/post/tests/work_offset_index.rs` (9 tests). Every shipped script runs on recorded streams at offsets 1, 6, 7, its maximum and one past it, checking the word it writes or the refusal by setup name. It also covers:
  - a recorded generator toolpath (`face_square_40x40.cl`) through Fanuc and Tormach;
  - legacy word streams posting byte-identically to their index;
  - invalid values;
  - an unflagged user script at 1-6 and at 7, and one that tries to raise its maximum;
  - a flagged script without a maximum or names;
  - the dump writing the index;
  - each script's name table.
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_refuses_a_work_offset_that_names_no_settable_frame` now expects the engine's refusal of `G53` (the engine refuses it before the script runs).
- Gate (local, worktree target, sccache), on head `2fe7afb7`:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
  - 63 app suites, 431 passed, 0 failed. They cover every app suite that posts through the shipped scripts: conformance, golden_cl, posting, arc_planes, cli, the probe_* suites, sinumerik_*, heidenhain_*, fanuc_post, doosan_dnm_post, carvera_*, tormach_*, the lathe_post* suites, plasma_*, inverted_*, comment_escape, one_wcs, setups, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, rotated_wcs, setup_mounts_post, setup_post_options, per_op_files, program_comments, smoothing, after_op, coolant*, post_unit_word, regression_models, wear_comp, control_comp and lathe_spindle_law. There are no separate mazak or haas suites; those scripts are covered by conformance, fanuc_post and the inverted_* suites.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- 400-line law: the new manifest reading lives in its own module, `work_offset.rs`. `engine.rs` (511 -> 530 lines) and `js.rs` (409 -> 415) were already over 400 and grew only by the hook-up.

**Goldens:** no golden file changed. Offsets 1-6 post the same words as before.

**Not exercised:** the GUI and MCP (unchanged in this slice), a real control, and offsets above 6 end to end through app (app still caps at 6 until slice 2).

Changelog: Posts receive the work offset as a 1-based number and write their own word; the Tormach mill and lathe posts accept work offsets 7-9 (G59.1-G59.3), and a post that cannot express an offset refuses it by setup name (#931, slice 1)

Refs #931

title: fix(thread): a matched thread mill verifies clean - the gouge laws read its major circle
body:
#1071: a Thread op's helix runs the thread depth H = 0.5413 x pitch past the declared hole, which is the thread's minor circle (what CAD draws of a tapped hole), by design (`machining2d::thread_mill`). The verify read that hole as a wall the cutter must keep `r` from, so every matched thread mill was blocked.

That covered the stock source too, which the issue thought was unaffected: the same thread from `SrcRef::Stock` had 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs. `mill2d_c` never asserted the warnings, so no thread mill could post from any source.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a (head ea76d5df).

## What changed

Three laws convicted a matched thread, and each is fixed narrowly.

- **Law (b), the rim.** The Thread arm now moves each declared hole's rim out to the major circle (declared radius + H), after the region is built (`material_source::major_rims`). This covers every source and the area-controlled region. A loop that is the hole's minor rim (ours, or the model's own for a through hole) gives way to it; every other wall stays.
- **The containment solid law.** It read the model's minor wall, and the face the hole opens through, as part to keep. A new `sim::verify::thread_bore` (and `solid_hits_threaded`) excuses a hit only when both of these hold:
  - the facet is the thread's own material: the minor wall (near-vertical, every vertex on the declared circle within max(2 % r, 0.1 mm)), or a facet with a vertex on that circle lying wholly at or above the hole's entry (the mouth);
  - the swept cutter stays inside the major cylinder: the farther tip end's radius plus the atom's radius is at most the major radius plus the allowance.

  Floors, walls of another radius, other holes and any cut past the major circle still convict. `solid_hits` is unchanged: it calls the threaded form with no bores.

  **Since the review of f122474d:** the band only RECOGNISES the wall. The cap reads the hit facet's own radius about the axis (its nearest on-circle vertex) plus the thread depth plus the allowance, not the declared major circle. A hole declared wider than, or off the centre of, the model's hole by more than the allowance now convicts. `major_rims` likewise grows a through hole's major circle from the model's own rim loop when that stands nearer than the declared circle.
  **Since the review of 434a464a:** the wall is measured at the facet's (or rim loop's) nearest point to the axis, not its nearest vertex. A chord between two on-circle vertices dips inside the circle.
  - That nearest point must itself be on the band, so a D-bore's flat, a coarse polygon's side, or a step reaching inside the mouth is never the thread's material.
  - The wall stands at that point, credited at most `CHORD_CREDIT` (the sim's `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm) toward its nearest vertex. That is tessellation of a round hole: the STEP importer meshes at half of it.
  - `major_rims` reads the same way. It moved with `thread_bores` into `operation/thread_rims.rs`, so `material_source.rs` stays at main's 350 lines.
- **Law (a), crossings.** The retract runs the ride backwards at feed. The reversed arcs put their chord joints a last bit off their twins, and `proper_cross` excused a touch only at an exactly zero orientation. So each shared joint, and each collinear overlap, read as a crossing.

  Now chords that only touch (an endpoint within 1 nm of the other chord's line) are no crossing. A real crossing keeps every endpoint off the other line. This is the one change that reaches every operation's verify, so the whole batch tier was run (below). A parallel-only guard was tried first: it removed 5 of the 21 pairs, and the rest were the joint touches.
- Two functions now take eight arguments (`SolidIndex::hits`, `contain_into`). They carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` with a reason, as ten others in `sim` already do.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1071-thread-mill-rim.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/thread_mill_rim.rs` (a 6 mm Tap-form thread mill, pitch 1, model-sourced unless named):
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_air_verifies_clean`: the issue's cavity fixture (#1073's block). Before the fix: 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs.
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_a_drilled_hole_verifies_clean`: a block with a real r 5 blind hole, 96-gon. Before the fix: the gouges came back from the solid law at the wall and the mouth.
  - `a_stock_sourced_thread_mill_verifies_clean_too`.
  - `a_thread_whose_major_circle_reaches_a_wall_convicts`: the major circle is 0.24 mm into the cavity wall; the minor circle is clear of it.
  - `a_thread_declared_wider_than_the_models_hole_convicts`: the model drilled r 4.5, declared r 5.
  - `a_thread_taken_below_the_models_hole_floor_convicts`: floor declared at Z 9, model floor at Z 10.
  - `a_declared_hole_wider_than_the_models_by_a_hair_convicts` (review round): r 5.05 / 5.1 on r 5, r 15.25 on r 15, and a through hole. It failed on f122474d.
  - `a_declared_hole_off_the_models_centre_by_a_hair_convicts` (review round): centres 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.28 mm off, blind and through. It failed on f122474d.
  - `a_matched_thread_stays_clean_at_other_sizes_and_through` (review round): matched r 15, a matched through hole, and a 5 um off-centre declaration.
  - `a_flat_whose_corners_stand_on_the_circle_convicts` (third review): a D-bore (flat from (3, 4) to (-3, 4)), an octagon and a 16-gon on r 5, and a through octagon. The D-bore verified with no warning on 434a464a, which was checked.
  - `a_fine_polygon_bore_still_verifies_clean` (third review): 48 and 96 sides on r 5.
- `sim::verify::thread_bore` unit tests: `a_flat_between_on_circle_corners_is_not_the_wall`, `a_tessellated_round_wall_reads_its_circle_and_a_coarse_one_its_chord`, `a_step_reaching_inside_the_mouth_is_not_the_mouth`.
- `crates/sim/tests/crossing_retrace.rs`:
  - `a_helix_run_back_over_its_own_trace_is_no_crossing`: three ride/retrace shapes, all-pairs and bucketed. It fails with the touch guard removed, which was checked.
  - `a_real_crossing_still_reads_as_one_at_any_angle`: 90 degrees down to 0.001 rad.

Gates:
- On the head ea76d5df (the third review's fix, merged with upstream main 62a2c93a):
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: every binary green (lib 89).
  - app `thread_mill_rim` 11, `verify` 21 (2 ignored), `mill2d_c` 9, `solid_law` 4, `solid_law_goldens` 5, `golden_cl` 25, `drill_prior` 12, `verify_arc_reading` 7, `bore_entry` 3, `bore_facet_sagitta` 2, `coarse_contain` 1, `ladder_entry_height` 4: all pass.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Review round 2, on the head 434a464a (upstream main 0fc30b65 merged cleanly, plus `turning: None` in the `thread_mill()` fixture for main's new `Tool.turning`, e1fc569a):
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test thread_mill_rim`: 9 passed.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --test crossing_retrace --test crossing_buckets`: 2 + 3 passed. `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib`: 86 passed.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test verify --test mill2d_c --test solid_law --test solid_law_goldens --test golden_cl --test drill_prior`: 21 (2 ignored) + 9 + 4 + 5 + 25 + 12 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- On the head d9b36d6a (the review fix, merged with upstream main c8a1bab1):
  - `cargo xtask gate batch`: geometry, cl, tools, sim, motion and ui green. The post step (`script_tormach_plasma`) and the app and clippy steps fail on main's own breaks, #1146: stale recorded plasma refusals, and the missing `Cutter::neck` field in `rotary_law_tests.rs`, which stops the app lib tests from compiling. This PR touches neither.
  - Because of that, every app integration suite was run separately: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test '*'`. Result: 297 suites, 2067 passed, 0 failed, 18 ignored.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test '*' -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Before the review round:
  - `cargo xtask gate batch` on c770b35c (18.3 min): every test suite green.
  - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim (with `crossing_buckets`), motion (slow suites included), app (`center_cut_multiaxis` included), ui.
  - clippy failed only on the two eight-argument functions. With the `#[allow]` (head commit), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- On the head, both pinning suites were rerun: green.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- No posted thread program was run on a machine or simulator.
- The thread flanks are not modelled: the whole minor-to-major annulus is read as removable (#986 owns the form).
- A tilted-frame (indexed) thread uses the same code path, but no test pins it.
- #1073's `coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_reads_the_same_near_the_bound_as_at_full_fidelity` lives on that open PR. When both land it can tighten to `== Vec::new()`, as #1071 asks.

Changelog: Thread milling: a thread mill matched to its hole verifies clean and can be posted. The gouge checks now read the thread's major circle, and the retract is no longer read as a crossing (#1071)

Effort: high (the issue's label). Not escalated.

Fixes #1071

title: feat(mcp): edit_tool - a partial tool patch through the undoable ChangeTool
body:
Stacked on #1076 (on #1070, #1060). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
New MCP tool `edit_tool {name, patch}` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tool_edit.rs`, registered in the tools table). `patch` is a partial tool definition in `add_tool`'s `definition` shape, applied as a JSON merge patch over the tool's current definition and run through the existing undoable `ChangeTool` (one undo step), so every ChangeTool gate refuses by tool name (retype stranding an op, bad cutting_data rows, catalog validation, sanity). Unknown keys are refused by name; `number`, `body` and `cutter` are refused by name too (other commands own them; see docs/decisions/1062-mcp-edit-tool.md). Operations on the tool go Stale as with a GUI edit. `lost`/`merge` in `mcp/edit.rs` became `pub(super)` for reuse.

title: test(gate): a motion generator change runs the operations suite
body:
## What

`crates/app/tests/operations.rs` generates every operation through the app layer, so its tests pin
the motion generators end to end — but its Gate map named `app::` modules only. A change under
`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/` therefore selected no suite that drives multiaxis rough end to end,
so `cargo xtask gate quick` could pass while
`multiaxis_rough_refuses_a_slot_the_cone_cannot_clear` sat out. PR #1044 hit exactly that: its gate
came out green and the failure surfaced only when a stacked merge ran the whole app list.

## The fix

- `operations.rs`'s Gate map names the generators its tests drive end to end, on top of main's
  crate-qualified mapping: `motion::machining3d`, `motion::multiaxis`, `motion::plunge_law` added
  (`motion::drilling`, `motion::finishing3d` and `motion::machining2d` are already there since the
  crate split).
- An xtask test in `xtask/src/gate_maps_tests.rs` (the real-checkout selection suite from #922)
  pins both halves: the map names every one of the six generators, and a plan for
  `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/mod.rs` selects `app:operations`. A header that loses a name now
  fails in xtask's own suite instead of in a later PR's gate run.

## Process

`xtask/` is a process file, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 41 → 42.

## How tested

- `cargo test -p xtask` — 56 passed (new test included)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` — ok (app operations suite 62 s, xtask 2 s)
- Selection proof: with a one-line probe under `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`,
  `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --plan` lists `app suites ... --test operations`;
  before the header change it listed motion suites only.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean

## Merge note

Main moved past this branch twice (the crate split, then further cuts). The branch now carries a
merge of `origin/main` (`6af3a4ca`), so the header keeps main's crate-qualified names and only adds
the three motion names above.

title: feat(fixtures): a rotary subplate on the plate grid raises the A centerline for the index swing
body:
**Stacked on #1020** (#818, `issue/818-swing-any-horizontal`): this branch starts from #1020's head, so until #1020 merges the diff below also shows its commit. Retarget/merge order per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack". Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Works #821 as corrected by its 2026-11-11 comment: the microARC subplate does **not** turn with A - it is a base plate that mounts the rotary on a fixture plate (two pin bores) or on the T-slots. The safety core: the index-swing check (#804/#810/#818) assumed the machine file's `nose_to_axis` (10.6 in, rotary on the bare table), which is unconservative once a plate and subplate raise the A centerline.

## What changed

- **Rotary subplate** = a new built-in accessory kind `rotary_subplate` (`Accessory::RotarySubplate`: length, width, thickness, bore spacing, first bore from -X, bores from -Y, bore diameter). Generic default figures, named generic (10 x 6 x 3/4 in, 1/2 in bores 6 in apart) - no maker's dimensions committed; the user enters theirs. Solid-slab mesh (bores drawn solid). It lands **fixed** (never in the swept radius). Its frame is the first pin bore at the underside, +X toward the second, so `PlaceOnPlate` seats it on a #819 dowel pair by its pins.
- **Pin law:** a subplate goes only on a dowel pair whose spacing equals its bore spacing (0.05 mm); a single hole or another spacing is refused by name - at `PlaceOnPlate`, at a `SetPlate` re-seat, and at a `SetAccessory` resize of the placed subplate (which also keeps its footprint on the plate).
- **Raised centerline** (`app::rotary_stack`): the setup's subplates and every plate under each (through the plate locations) form a stack; the tallest one is used. The swing clause judges with the **effective** `nose_to_axis` = machine figure less the stack, or the setup's **stated** figure, which wins.
- **Refusal law:** a stack whose thickness is unknown (an imported plate under the subplate, a vanished or looped plate, a non-finite figure), a stated figure that is no length, or an effective figure at or under zero refuses the swing **by name** - never judged on the table figure. **No subplate: judged word for word as before** (pinned by the exact message).
- **Per-setup stated figure:** `SetupDef::nose_to_axis`, command `SetSetupNoseToAxis` (finite, > 0, <= 5000 mm; no-op refused; undoable), carried by a datum transfer with the machine.
- **Save/load:** additive setup key `nose_to_axis`; the subplate rides the existing `accessory` key. Old files load unchanged (pinned).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/821-rotary-on-plate-stack.md`.

## Commands, MCP, UI

- Commands: `InsertAccessory` / `SetAccessory` (new kind), `PlaceOnPlate` (pin law), new `SetSetupNoseToAxis`.
- MCP: `add_accessory` / `set_accessory` take `rotary_subplate`; `place_on_plate` applies the pin law; new `get_rotary_stack` (stack layers, stated figure, machine rotaries, refusal reason) and `set_setup_nose_to_axis` (number or null).
- UI: the Fixtures page's accessory dialog lists "Rotary subplate" (KINDS-driven); the setup's Machine page gets a "Rotary centerline" section (machine figure, the stack readout or the refusal, a checkbox + field for the setup's stated figure, queued as `CommandKind::SetupNoseToAxis`). Drawn only for a machine with a work-turning rotary. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Tests

title: fix(app,motion): judge probe and plasma on a reduced-fidelity model; cone/engrave rides stay refused
body:
Stacked on #1064 (base it on main once #1064 merges; it carries #1064's commits until then).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed, per kind

#904 left five kinds refused outright on any reduced-fidelity model. Same rule as #864/#904: a law gives the model's excess back out of its slack while a positive slack is left (`verify::excess_floor`); past that it reads untightened and the program gate refuses the op by name.

- **Probe - now judged.** Both halves of the protected-move law read `probe_op::stylus_slack(excess)` = `STYLUS_SLACK` less the excess: the ball distance law (`stylus_hits_excess`) and the stem/body solid law (`stylus_reach_hits_excess`). The old functions forward with 0, so existing callers don't change. `generate` passes `material.excess`. Nothing else judges a probe against the model.
- **Plasma - now judged.** The kerf law (part grown by `kerf/2 - tol`, which the lead planner reads too) and the cover law read `PlasmaParams::kerf_tol()` = `KERF_TOL` less the new `PlasmaParams::model_excess`. `plasma_op` fills that field from `material.excess`. The cut-order, crossing and tip-up laws read only the path.
- **`fidelity_law`**: `excess_aware` now accepts Probe and every Plasma kind. `floor_of` also lists each kind's own slack (`own_law_tol_of`). `GOUGE_TOL` stays the base, so plasma is still refused at 0.01 mm of excess, which is stricter than its 0.025 mm law needs.
- **Cone rides (2D chamfer, deburr) and engrave rides (trace, engrave) - still refused, with the reason recorded.** No law holds them to a tolerance against the model: the ride *is* the mesh edge by construction, so there's no tolerance to give back. Deburr also reads bends between coarse facets as creases. Judging them would need a new stated ride accuracy, which is open design, not a tightening. The reason is in `fidelity_law`'s header and the decision file.
- **Cross drill - still refused; #1053 stays open for it (hence `Refs`).** Its part law and `rapids_radial` would each take a one-line tightening. But the chain is also proved by zero-slack readings of the mesh: `cross_stock::standoff` / `rapids_clear`, `cross_entry`, and `drill_reach`'s reach and holder faces. Tightening those means growing each measured standoff by the excess, which moves the kernel's stations. As #904 set, a law isn't tightened for a kind that stays refused.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1053-fidelity-probe-plasma.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/coarse_probe_plasma.rs`. Each law is pinned so that a reading between the plain and the tightened slack is convicted only on the coarse model (excess 0.007), and a real hit is convicted on both:
- `a_ball_between_the_slacks_is_a_gouge_only_on_the_coarse_model`: a touch 0.006 mm in; a real gouge at 0.05 mm.
- `a_stem_between_the_slacks_is_a_shank_hit_only_on_the_coarse_model`: an overhang lip 0.006 mm into the stem; a real hit at 0.05 mm.
- `the_probe_op_judges_with_its_models_excess`: the same lip through `GenerateOperation` on an import with no flag and one flagged 0.012 mm. This proves the wiring.
- `a_kerf_between_the_tolerances_is_refused_only_on_the_coarse_model`: the part grown 0.02 mm past the cut outline; the kerf law refuses by name. A real reach at 0.1 mm is refused on both.
- `the_stylus_slack_...` and `the_kerf_tolerance_gives_the_excess_back_and_reads_plain_past_the_bound`: past the bound the laws read their plain slack.
- `probe_and_plasma_are_judged_while_a_tolerance_is_left_and_refused_by_name_past_it`, plus `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`, whose refused list loses Probe and PlasmaProfile: judged at 0.012 mm, refused by name at 0.030 mm.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws`) and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the final head: green on 2e4058e7 (motion lib 31 s, 52 app suites 156 s, golden_cl plasma 1 s; 0 failed); clippy -D warnings clean.

## Not exercised

- The plasma cover law's tightening has no marginal pin. Its reading compares the path with the contour, and no fixture puts an edge between 0.018 and 0.025 mm past `kerf` on demand.
- There's no document-level plasma fixture. The part region comes from the model's silhouette slice, which can't be grown by a chosen 0.02 mm, so the law is pinned through `plasma_profile`.
- A bore touch on a coarse model: the tightened slack convicts a tangent touch once the excess passes ~0.0025 mm, because the bore's facets stand inside it. That's a false gouge on the safe side, the #1057 shape, and is recorded in the decision file.

No goldens or snapshots moved (`golden_cl::plasma_plate_with_holes_matches_golden` passes with `model_excess: 0.0`).

Changelog: Probe and Plasma Profile operations can now post from a reduced-fidelity model (e.g. a metre-unit STEP file); their collision laws are tightened by the model's excess and refuse by name past it (#1053)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #1053

title: fix(motion): microlift pieces take longer chords only where they leave no sliver
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 3e9b8ae1; upstream/main a6bd69d8, with #1032, merged in at 6ccef5e4). **Stacked on #1007** (`issue/983-rings-fallback-note`, merged into this branch at 1eff2424: it gives the rotary level reader the ladder's step on the same line of the r6.2 pin this PR rewrites). Until #1007 merges, its commits show in this diff; this PR's own change is commit 42ee5e38 (plus the decision note f23ebc3c).

## What changed

The microlift acceptance (`adaptive/lift.rs`, `lift_returns`) compared the lifted plan's worst reading with the spiral's and flipped on nanometres. It was not a rounding tie: readings are whole rim samples (half degrees), and the extra sample was real. A piece re-thinned to longer chords (0.01 mm sag) cuts inside the arc it replaces and leaves a sliver on the stock side; the next piece meets it as one or two samples the spiral never planned, and which planner cells the sliver covers turns on nanometres of ring geometry.

- `lift_coarse::cut` (new module, `coarsen` moved into it): a piece takes its longer chords only where they read within the bound **and** leave standing no cell its own chords clear (`Raster::stands_over`). Otherwise it is cut on its own chords, the spiral's.
- `lift::keeps`: the acceptance keeps its law, with **no tolerance**. A lifted plan that reads over the spiral (or over the bound, where the spiral read under it) is never kept. The stated tolerance is zero.
- No other planner file is touched (`grow.rs`, PR #953's, and `budget.rs` are as they were).

Why not the tolerance the issue asked for: a one-sample tolerance posts a plan that reads over the stated bound, and two samples are needed (48.5 was read). The decision file has the alternatives: `docs/decisions/982-microlift-acceptance.md`.

## Readings (release, Linux x86-64)

60 x 14 slot, D10, bound 47.5014 deg; lifted / spiral reading. "Opening" is `rings::open` eroding that much deeper than it dilates back, "width" the slot that much wider.

| twin | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unperturbed | 47.5 / 47.5 kept | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| opening 8, 32, 48 nm | 48.0 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| opening 180 nm | 48.5 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| width -125, -62, -8, +32, +510 nm | 48.0 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| width +8 nm | 48.5 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| the other 19 twins (opening 16 nm - 1 um, width -250 nm - +5 um) | kept | kept |

Before, 10 of 30 twins dropped the lifted plan. After, 0 of 30, each reading its worst where the spiral does (the first turn out of the entry bore).

Cost: the `adaptive_hsm` narrow slot posts 14 534 moves instead of 13 378 (+8.6 %; a third of its pieces keep longer chords instead of two thirds); cut and air lengths within 3 mm; load, breaks and verdict unchanged. Planning time unchanged.

## The one fixture verdict that changes

The issue's Done-means asks that no adaptive fixture's verdict change. One does, and has to: `rotary_adaptive`'s r6.2 neck levels (5.7, 5.2), pinned "refused for travel" since #55. That verdict was this same coin. On unchanged main, openings perturbed only:

| opening | radius 5.7 | radius 5.2 | old pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0, 8, 125 nm | rings | rings | green |
| 16, 62 nm | **HSM-planned** | rings | red |
| 250, 510 nm | rings | **HSM-planned** | red |

After the fix both levels read 47.5 / 47.5 and are HSM-planned on microlift returns at every perturbation tried (0, 16, 32, 250 nm). The pin is rewritten: `the_r62_neck_levels_are_hsm_planned_on_microlift_returns`. They were cut by Offset rings at 100 % D with 15-21 breaks of 45-135 deg; they now read 20.3 % D on the suite's 0.1 mm dexel, no planner overload. Two readings are pinned as read, not at the whole bar's laws, and appear on main too whenever the coin lands the other way: 20.3 % D at the first turn out of the entry bore (law 19.8 %), and three breaks of 5.1-5.5 deg on radius 5.2. Filed as #1050.

Every other verdict is unchanged: bore, rectangle, L-pocket, island, narrow slot, channel (`adaptive_hsm`), the band (`adaptive_band`), `pocket3d_hsm`, `level_links`, the other `rotary_adaptive` tests.

## Goldens

None moves. `tests/golden/` holds no HSM plan, and no digest pins a lifted plan. Posted programs of lifted plans do change (more pieces on their own chords).

## How tested

Pinning tests (all fail without the sliver check; the first two were run that way):
- `adaptive::tests::the_slot_and_its_32_nm_twin_decide_the_same_way` (default lane)
- `adaptive::lift_tests::a_piece_takes_longer_chords_only_where_they_leave_no_sliver` (default lane)
- `adaptive::lift_tests::the_lifted_plan_is_kept_only_at_or_under_the_spiral_reading` (default lane; the zero tolerance)
- `adaptive::tests::the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations` (heavy lane: 20 twins, 8 nm - 0.51 um)
- `rotary_adaptive::the_r62_neck_levels_are_hsm_planned_on_microlift_returns` (heavy lane, rewritten)

Gate, on the final head 6ccef5e4: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green, 0 failed, wall 4.7 min (every motion suite ran: the stack touches a shared test fixture). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Release `--include-ignored` (heavy lanes): motion lib 198/198 (the 20-twin sweep included), `adaptive_hsm` 6/6, `adaptive_band` 2/2, `rotary_adaptive` 6/6, `pocket3d_hsm` 4/4, `level_links` 12/12, `adaptive_orbit_seam` 1/1 (on 6ccef5e4). App (release, `--include-ignored`, on 42ee5e38): `roughing2d` 7/7, `shoulder_adaptive` 3/3, `pocket_overhead` 2/2, `whole_model_pocket` 5/5, `stock_engine_agreement` 3/3.

## What was not exercised

- **Windows and macOS.** Everything above is Linux x86-64. The planner's output differs in the last bits between platforms (#1010), so which twins flipped before differs there (the first worker saw 32 nm flip on Apple silicon); the fix does not depend on which.
- **The app's STEP bore count pin** (`pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`, re-pinned per platform by #1032): on Linux it reads (16196, 15457, 1570) with and without this change, inside #1032's band for unmeasured platforms, so the exact Windows and macOS triples are not expected to move - but they were not measured. (Before #1032 it read (6490, 6454, 222) on Linux both ways.) A reviewer on Windows or macOS: the test prints its triple.
- The rotary suite under perturbation beyond the r6.2 pin: the r7 bar's and the window's deepest levels flip on the #850 planning budget (main and this branch alike; the r7 pin is red with the openings 250 nm deeper on both). Filed as #1051.
- #882's held speedup was not re-measured on top of this.
- Debug-profile runs of the heavy lanes; UI; batch tier.

Changelog: Adaptive: a microlifted piece is posted on longer chords only where they leave no sliver of stock, so the lifted plan no longer flips to the bare spiral (and the pocket to Offset rings) on nanometre changes of the geometry; the rotary r6.2 neck levels are HSM-planned on microlift returns instead of ring-cut.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #982

title: feat(pick): box-select edge chains and faces into an operation's picks
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main a6bd69d8).

## What changed

- **Viewport box select** (`crates/ui/src/box_pick.rs`, `egui_app/shell.rs`): Ctrl (or Shift) + left drag in Edge or Face mode, with an operation open and no other pick draft collecting, draws a rubber band instead of orbiting. On release it adds every visible feature edge chain (Edge mode) or welded face (Face mode) in the box to the operation's picks, as **one `SetOperationGeometry`**, so it is one undo step. A drag to the right is a **window** (takes only what lies wholly inside), a drag to the left is a **crossing** box (also takes what it touches). The band is solid for a window and dashed for a crossing box. A plain left drag still orbits.
- **The rule** (`crates/app/src/pick/box_pick.rs`: `box_bodies`, `box_select`, `box_select_top`) follows #692's one pick rule. Only feature chains are candidates (never facet seams). A candidate counts only if part of it is unoccluded from the eye, using the click pick's own sight test (`feature_pick::occluded`, now `pub(super)`, with no behaviour change), at most 16 sight rays per candidate. It honours the viewport's Pick through toggle (`state.pick_through`) as a click does: off, hidden features stay out; on, they are taken too. Only parts are candidates, never stock or fixtures, but stock and fixtures still hide what lies behind them.
- **MCP**: new tool `pick_in_box` (`crates/app/src/mcp/box_pick.rs`). It takes a world X/Y box seen from straight above (the Top view, orthographic), with `mode` window/crossing and `kind` chains/faces. By default it adds to the current picks; `replace: true` replaces them. One undo step. An empty, degenerate or already-picked box is refused with a message that names the reason. `mcp::pick::kind_door` is now `pub(super)` so the new tool can reuse it.
- The Selection row's hover text documents the gesture. Decisions are in `docs/decisions/979-box-select-picks.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/box_pick.rs` uses a 100 x 60 x 10 plate with two square through-cutouts:
  - `a_window_around_one_cutout_takes_exactly_its_top_rim`: from the top in ortho, exactly the cutout's 4 top-rim chains. In perspective, straight over the hole, the eye sees into it, so the result is 12 chains, all on that cutout.
  - `a_window_around_everything_takes_every_top_rim_chain_and_no_hidden_one`: 12 top-rim chains (outer + 2 cutouts), all at the top. Pick-through gives 36 (the hidden ones exist). Seen from below, only the bottom rims.
  - `a_crossing_box_takes_what_it_touches_a_window_only_what_it_holds`
  - `faces_box_the_same_way_and_hidden_faces_stay_out`
  - `degenerate_boxes_take_nothing`
  - `mcp_pick_in_box_adds_the_rim_in_one_undo_step`: covers two boxes and two undos, `replace`, and refusals.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/box_select.rs` drives real egui pointer and modifier events on the seeded shell with the plate imported, Top view, ortho:
  - `a_ctrl_drag_window_around_one_cutout_adds_its_rim_in_one_undo_step`: no orbit, exactly 4 chains appended to Contour1, and one Undo restores the seed's pick.
  - `a_right_to_left_drag_is_a_crossing_box_and_a_plain_drag_still_orbits`
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green on 6716fad1 (app suites 27 s incl. box_pick, feature_pick, mcp_pick; ui lib + 10 suites 17 s)

## Not exercised

- The real-window (winit/wgpu) look of the rubber band. Only the kittest harness drew it. No snapshot PNG changed.
- The user's actual cutouts project from #241. It is not in the repo, so the plate fixture stands in for it.
- Very large meshes: the cost is up to 16 sight rays per in-box candidate, each against every facet. It was not timed on a 1M-facet model.
- The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table gains the `pick_in_box` row (with `through`); `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` bumped 43 -> 44 (the number is taken at merge time).

Changelog: Viewport box select - Ctrl/Cmd+drag in Edge/Face mode adds every visible edge chain or face in the box to the open operation's picks in one undo step (drag right: window, left: crossing), hidden ones too while Pick through is on; MCP `pick_in_box` does the same from the Top view, with an optional `through` (#979)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #979

title: feat(tools): a tool carries cutting data per workpiece material
body:
Stacked on #1070 (on #1060). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- `Tool` gains `cutting: Vec<CuttingRow>` (new `camcraft_tools::cutting_rows`). Each row is `{material, rpm, feed}`, keyed by the built-in `WorkMaterial` groups the document's material already uses. The tool's own `rpm`/`feed` stay the running numbers the post reads, and the fallback.
- Seeding happens only through commands, one undo step each:
  - `SetWorkMaterial` re-seeds every tool that has a row for the new material (`ChangeTool`), plus the milling feed of each op on such a tool (`EditOperationParams`). The status line says how many moved.
  - `AddTool` starts on the document material's row.
  - A `ChangeTool` that edits only the table loads the row. An Apply that also states rpm/feed keeps its own numbers.
  - `EditOperationLinks` (tool retarget) takes the new tool's row feed.
  - Quick-add, MCP `add_operation` and the recognizer seed a new op's feed. An explicit MCP params patch still wins.
- **Nothing moves on load.** With no matching row, everything stays as it is today.
- File: an additive `cutting_data` key on `ToolDto`, written only when the tool has rows. A tool without rows saves byte-identical, so there is no version step. An unknown material word refuses the file by name.
- Validation by tool name at `AddTool`/`ChangeTool` (and `is_sane` at read): rpm and feed must be finite and above zero (a torch row states rpm 0), and no material may appear twice.
- Tool editor: a new collapsed "Cutting data by material" header (`tool_cutting_rows.rs`) with per-row material, rpm, feed, Remove, and "Add material row". The Body column is untouched (#1043).
- MCP: `add_tool`'s `definition` takes `cutting_data`, and `get_job` shows it. Stating the material over MCP is still #732; editing a tool is #1062.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/890-cutting-data-per-material.md`, including the #1060 interaction: Update/Replace still match by name and import rows and running numbers as the library states them, with no re-seed.

## How tested
Pinning tests, all in `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs`:
- `a_tool_without_rows_writes_no_key_and_a_table_round_trips`
- `a_project_without_rows_saves_byte_identical_and_a_table_survives_save_load`

Also unit tests `cutting_rows::tests` (tools) and `tool_cutting_rows::tests::rows_add_per_material_and_ride_the_draft_both_ways` (ui).

title: fix(sim,app): read a containment kind's declared rim at the plain gouge tolerance on a reduced-fidelity model
body:
Stacked on #1064 (branch `issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws`: this uses its `verify/excess.rs` split and its `coarse_contain` fixture). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## Root cause

A Z drill, bore or thread mill verifies (`Mode::Boundary`) against rim loops that are our own polygons of each hole's declared circle (`material_source::rim_loop`), built to `RIM_SAG_BUDGET` = 0.005 mm, half the 0.01 mm `GOUGE_TOL`. A 2 mm rim (48 sides) stands 0.00428 mm inside its circle, so a matched drill reads `r - 0.00428` off it. #864 had law (b) read **every** loop at `GOUGE_TOL - excess`. Past 0.01 - 0.00428 = 0.00572 mm of excess (a model flagged above ~0.0107 mm; the issue saw 0.0105 clean, 0.011 convicted) the tolerance left no longer covered the rim's own sagitta: `Gouge { at: 1 }` on a matched drill, and on every ring of a matched bore. Past 0.015 mm `excess_floor` reads untightened and the gate refuses by name, which is why 0.03 read clean.

## What changed

- `sim::verify::VerifyContext` gets `rims: &[(Point2, f64)]` (empty by default): the declared circles of a containment kind. `VerifyContext::is_rim` / `loop_tol` (in `verify/excess.rs`) match a loop to one (every vertex within 2 um: the region's 1 um lattice snap).
- Law (b) (`verify/section.rs`), both the law-point reading and the Boundary whole-move wall reading, reads a rim loop at the plain `gouge_tol` and every other loop at `tightened(gouge_tol)` as before. Rims are found once per verify call.
- `app::operation::generate` fills `rims` from the Drill (Z holes) and Bore params (Thread declares none, see below) when the depth law is `Contain` (`material_source::rims_of`), at both verify sites.
- The solid law against the model's facets (`contain_into`) is untouched and still tightened.

Why the plain tolerance is honest: the excess measures how far a coarse model's facets stand inside its true surface; a rim is not a facet but a circle we draw from the hole's own centre and radius, so the rim's reading is exactly today's full-fidelity verdict. Nothing a full-fidelity model convicts is acquitted. Decision file: `docs/decisions/1057-drill-excess-false-gouge.md` (options dropped: finer rims, exact-circle reading, zeroing the excess for the containment kinds, recognising rims structurally in sim).

## Readings (`coarse_rims` fixture: 40x40x20 block, 20x20 cavity blind at Z 10, DR-0400 to Z 10.2)

| flagged | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| full, 0.008, 0.0105 | clean | clean |
| 0.011, 0.012, 0.0149 | `Gouge { at: 1 }` | clean |
| 0.03 | clean + refused by name | clean + refused by name |

Matched bore (EM-0800-4FL in a 6 mm-radius hole) at 0.011 / 0.0149: before `Gouge { at: 6, 7, 8, 17, ... }`, after clean.

## How tested

Pinning tests (all fail before the fix where they name a false conviction, pass after):
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_drill_is_clean_on_a_model_flagged_anywhere_below_the_refusal_bound` (full, 0.008, 0.0105, 0.011, 0.012, 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_bore_is_clean_near_the_refusal_bound` (+ a bore offset 1 mm into the wall still convicts at 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::the_real_drill_gouges_still_convict_on_a_model_near_the_refusal_bound` (oversize drill, drill offset into the wall, drill 0.5 mm past the floor - each at full, 0.011 and 0.0149; and 0.005 mm past the floor: clean at full fidelity, a gouge at 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_drill_past_the_bound_is_refused_by_name_not_convicted` (0.03: no warnings, the gate's fidelity line by name)
- `coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_on_a_coarse_model_is_never_read_looser_than_at_full_fidelity`
- `model_excess::a_declared_rim_is_read_untightened_and_no_other_loop_is` (sim: an undeclared rim convicted near the bound, declared clean, a 2.01 drill still convicted, a declaration that does not trace the loop leaves the coarse boss convicted)

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws` on the final head fe7403bc - sim 9 s, motion 4 s, app 201 s, 0 failed (3.6 min); plus `verify` and `mill2d_c` (rim law and bore/thread from stock) green; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. No goldens or snapshot PNGs moved.

## Not exercised

- Thread declares no rim (#1073 review): since #1071 its region reads the major circle (`thread_rims::major_rims`), so a minor declaration traced no loop. A thread mill on a coarse model keeps the tightened reading (conservative) and may convict near the refusal bound where full fidelity is clean; declaring the major circle is a follow-up.
- The 3+2 framed verify site passes the same rims; a rim drawn in the local frame that does not match the world-frame circles simply falls back to the tightened reading (today's behaviour). Not exercised by a framed fixture.

Changelog: A drill or bore matched to its hole is no longer falsely convicted of a gouge on a model imported between ~0.0105 mm and the 0.015 mm refusal bound (#1057, PR #1073)

Fixes #1057

title: fix(turning): judge a lathe holder body against chuck jaws and standing steel
body:
Stacked on #1043 (branch `issue/361-vendor-tool-models` on the mkinney fork). Upstream cannot base a PR on a fork branch, so this targets `main` and its diff shows #1043's commits as well. Merge #1043 first; after that, this PR's own diff is the single commit c965895f.

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A turning tool's lathe holder body (#369) was judged against the part and the stock only. The fixture laws swept the tool record's holder cylinder, which is 0 x 0 for a turning insert. So an offset holder running into a chuck jaw passed with no finding, while the op had dropped its "holder not judged" note because a body was present (P0: a holder hitting the chuck is a crash).

- **New law, `operation/turning_holder_steel.rs`.** Each move's meridian pieces (the holder law's own `pieces_of`) are read against every fixture box with each of the body's clearance spans (`LatheClearance::spans`). A strike is `FixtureHit { fixture_part: Holder }` on that move ("holder at move N strikes a fixture"), which blocks the post.
  - Steel that turns with the part (a chuck jaw, the fixture default) is read as its revolved envelope.
  - Standing steel (`SetFixtureFixed`: tailstock, steady rest, table) is a box in the machine frame: station, radial in the plane the moves are written in, and across that plane. The band keeps only |y|, so both sides are read.
  - For a straight tip motion each condition is an interval of the piece's parameter, so strikes are found exactly, not sampled. Boxes grow by the gouge tolerance (contact is contact, as in the fixture laws).
- **Same law at the post gate.** `fixture_struck::op_hits` (the live fixture walk and the struck-fixture view) runs it too, reading the op's part as generation does and the steel as it stands now. A part it cannot read is reported unjudged by name.
- **Unreadable steel is named.** A tagged fixture with no readable geometry has no box, and every box law passes over it. A bodied turning op now carries a note naming it (`STEEL_UNREAD_NOTE`, from `fixture::unreadable_for`).
- `turning_holder::pieces_of` is now `pub(super)`. `SignedMeridian` gains `suv` (station, radial, across-plane).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1037-lathe-holder-steel.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, `crates/app/tests/turning_holder_steel.rs`:
- `an_offset_holder_reaching_a_chuck_jaw_blocks_naming_the_move`: an L holder whose leg stands clear of the part reaches a chuck jaw. There is no HolderHit; there is a holder FixtureHit, the post is refused naming the move, and the live gate walk gives the same moves.
- `the_same_holder_short_of_the_jaw_passes_and_posts`
- `a_standing_jaw_is_read_in_the_machine_frame_and_a_spinning_one_about_the_axis`: a jaw beside the tool's plane is struck while it spins and is clear once declared fixed. In the plane, fixed, it is struck.
- `a_fixture_the_law_cannot_read_is_named_on_the_op`
- Unit test: `operation::turning_holder_steel::tests::a_band_meets_a_box_exactly_along_a_straight_tip_motion`.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/361-vendor-tool-models`) green: the app suites (lib plus 120 suites, the new one included, 629 s) and 6 ui suites (116 s), 0 failed. By hand, also green: `turning_insert_zone`, `vendor_tool_body`, `mcp_tool_body`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `sim_tool_body`, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`. After a final prefilter edit (skip steel the body's length cannot reach), `turning_holder_steel`, `turning_holder`, `fixtures`, `vendor_tool_body`, the lib unit tests and clippy were run again: green. No golden or snapshot changed.

## Not exercised

- Real vendor chuck or tailstock models: only box fixtures. A mesh fixture is read by its box (conservative; the mesh acquittal of #339 is not applied to this law).
- A spindle off a world axis: the reading there is conservative by construction, but no test covers it.
- GUI: no new UI. The finding shows through the existing fixture-hit paths.

## Overlap

#904 (reduced-fidelity turning/rotary/multiaxis laws) is in flight on main. This PR adds a module and one call after the holder law in `generate.rs`, and touches `turning_holder.rs` only to make `pieces_of` visible.

Changelog: A lathe holder body is judged against the setup's workholding: a chuck jaw as its revolved envelope, standing steel (tailstock, steady rest) in the machine frame, a strike blocking the post by move; a fixture with no readable geometry is named on the op (#1037)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #1037

title: feat(tools): place a lathe holder body from the tool editor and MCP
body:
Makes a lathe holder body reachable: the tool editor and the MCP server can now give a turning tool a holder from a STEP, STL or OBJ file, placed in the turning tool frame. The judging law (#369) and its insert zone (#396) already existed, but nothing a user could reach led to them.

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 3e9b8ae1).

## Where #361 stood

The triage split (#368, #369, #370, #371) has all shipped. What was missing is the case the issue names first, asymmetric lathe tooling:

- The tool editor placed every body along a spindle axis, so Apply body on a turning tool was refused with "lathe holders are placed in the turning tool frame" and the GUI had no way to do that.
- The MCP server had no tool-body tool; the camcraft-mcp skill listed it as a known gap.

## What changed

- **Tool editor.** On a lathe-held tool the Body section places the imported file in the turning tool frame: radial and spindle directions (a preset or a picked face normal), the tip (numbers or a picked corner) and an optional insert zone. Apply body queues the existing `SetToolBody::lathe`, one undo step. A boring bar, which serves both machines, gets a frame switch. Milling tools are unchanged.
- **MCP.** Five tools in `crates/app/src/mcp/body_tools.rs`: `get_tool_body`, `set_tool_body` (by numbers, or by a STEP's ISO 13399 coordinate systems), `set_lathe_tool_body`, `set_lathe_insert_zone`, `clear_tool_body`. Each write is one `SetToolBody`.
- **Safety: a reduced-fidelity STEP is refused as a tool body.** Every body-file path used `load_model`, which drops #864's chord error. A coarsely meshed holder reads smaller than the holder is, so its collision checks were too generous with nothing said. All body files now pass one door (`tool_body_file`), which refuses such a file by name and says to simplify the model. This touches only the tool-body readers, not the part laws #904 is working on.
- **Process.** The camcraft-mcp skill lists the new tools and drops the gap; `PROCESS_VERSION` 16 -> 17.
- **Fixture.** `testdata/models/lathe_holder_offset.step` is our own extruded L (an offset holder), written by a small script. No vendor file was read or committed.

No new judging law and no change to posted output for existing documents. Decisions are in `docs/decisions/361-vendor-tool-models.md`.

## How tested

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) green on 1a6d4017: 26 app suites and the ui lib plus 10 ui suites, 0 failed. Also run and green: `tool_body`, `turning_holder`, `tool_csys`, `turning_insert_zone`, `holder_library`, `tool_body_judged`, `tool_body_bands`, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/vendor_tool_body.rs`
  - `a_step_lathe_holder_placed_off_its_model_frame_is_judged_and_its_mirror_stands_clear`: the STEP holder rubs the part's shoulder (3.2 mm short, post blocked); the same file with the spindle direction reversed is clear.
  - `a_step_meshed_coarser_than_promised_is_refused_as_a_tool_body_by_name`: all five file doors refuse.
  - `the_lathe_placement_preview_is_the_commands_own_reading`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_tool_body.rs` (5 tests): both frames, the insert zone, undo/redo, and every refusal by name.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_body_lathe.rs` (6 tests): Apply body lands one undoable command, a non-square placement and an oversized zone are refused by name, picks fill only the draft, the boring bar's frame switch, the coarse-STEP refusal at import.

I also rendered the editor once at 1280x720 to check the lathe section fits; no snapshot PNG is changed.

## Not exercised

- No real vendor STEP was tried (none may be committed, and none was used); the fixture is eight planar faces.
- The picks were tested through the state calls, not by clicking the 3D preview.
- No hands-on run of the GUI beyond the one rendered frame.
- Inch documents: the lathe fields use the same unit lens as the other fields, but no test types an inch value into them.

## Still owed on #361

- #1037 (P1): the lathe holder body is judged against part and stock only, not workholding or fixtures.
- #1038: the lathe body is not drawn in the simulation or viewport.
- #1039: a lathe placement from a file's ISO 13399 coordinate systems.
- #1040: a tool assembled from several vendor bodies (the ISO 26622 / 26623 interfaces the issue names).
- #1041: judge a reduced-fidelity body grown by its chord error instead of refusing it.
- Imported bodies in `.camtools` library files ride #889.

Changelog: Lathe holder bodies from the tool editor and MCP: a turning tool's STEP holder is placed in the turning tool frame (directions, tip, insert zone); MCP `get_tool_body`, `set_tool_body`, `set_lathe_tool_body`, `set_lathe_insert_zone`, `clear_tool_body`; a STEP too detailed to mesh at full fidelity is refused as a tool body (#361)

title: fix(post): a touch probe section starts no coolant on any mill post
body:
Stacked on #961 (branch `issue/869-coolant-air`; this PR's own change is the top commit, 5d8b71e2). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
A touch probe section (a section that states a speed of 0, the #523 / #574 test) now starts no coolant on any shipped mill post - no M7 / M8 / M88 at its start, so no M9 / M89 for it at its end - whatever the op's coolant ask and whether or not the machine states coolant codes.

- `fanuc`, `haas`, `sinumerik`, `heidenhain`, `mazak`: `coolant = probeStop ? "" : coolantFor(coolantAsk);` (reusing the existing #574 `probeStop`).
- `doosan-dnm`: same gate on a new `touchProbe` (this post posted M8 for a probe even with no machine).
- `carvera`: same gate (it posts no probing, but the law holds).
- `tormach`: already gated (#108 / #362), unchanged.

Fixed in the posts, not the stream: `post::dump` does not know a section is a probe, the TOUCH / FOUND records arrive after the preamble, `tormach.cps` reads no `PARAM Coolant` (a stream-side `Coolant off` would be refused there), and a recorded probe stream with no `PARAM Coolant` would still post flood. An explicit Mist / Air / Through-tool ask on a probe op is neither posted nor refused. Why, and what was dropped: `docs/decisions/995-probe-no-coolant.md`.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_no_coolant.rs` (5 tests, every mill post): `a_probe_section_starts_no_coolant_on_a_machine_that_states_coolants`, `a_probe_section_starts_no_coolant_without_a_machine`, `a_probe_section_ignores_an_explicit_coolant_ask`, `a_bore_centre_probe_posts_no_coolant_on_doosan_dnm` (the issue's TOUCH-record probe stream, with and without `doosan-dnm.mch`), and the control `a_cutting_section_still_starts_its_coolant`. 4 of the 5 fail on #961's posts, the control passes on both.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/869-coolant-air`: green. Since `.cps` changes are not gate-mapped, 47 app suites touching posts / probing / coolant were run by hand (fanuc_post, conformance, carvera_post, doosan_dnm_post, probe_op, probe_dialects, probe_tormach, probe_guard, probe_spindle_stop, coolant, coolant_air, coolant_followups, heidenhain_cycles, inverted_post, inverted_probe, posting, tormach_post, ...): all green. clippy on the new suite: clean.
- Goldens moved: none. Every committed probe golden is posted machine-less, where only Doosan posted coolant, and Doosan has no committed probe golden.

title: fix(xtask): quick maps a #[path]-included file to its parent's submodule
body:
Stacked on #972 (which stacks on #967 and #965). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
`cargo xtask gate quick` now also maps a source file that a sibling includes with `#[path = "x.rs"] mod name;` to `(parent, name)`, the module the compiler sees. This is a union with the file's own name, so it never selects fewer suites. Before, it took the file name as a top-level module. `crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs` is `app::posting::index_swing`, and the suites already name it `app::posting (index_swing)` correctly. The plan read it as `app::posting_index_swing`, which no map names, so a change to the index-swing safety law selected no suites.

- New `xtask/src/path_mods.rs` (`included_as`), hooked into `quick::plan`.
- It covers every `#[path]` file in the tree (posting's nine siblings, stock_sim, drill_reach, ui state, ...) without touching any suite header.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1021-path-included-modules.md`. Fixing the plan rather than renaming the maps, which were right.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` → 20, because xtask is a process file. A fork needs nothing beyond the normal process sync.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 44 passed. After review, the pin also asserts that posting_sim still selects wall_column_gouge and contour_arc_sim, posting_suppressed selects rest_across_setups, and posting_plasma selects plasma_gate.
- Earlier pin text: The new pin is `gate_maps_tests::a_path_included_file_selects_its_parents_submodule_suites`: a change to `posting_index_swing.rs` selects `index_swing`, narrows below all of `app::posting`, and the other posting siblings select suites.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Not exercised: #1020's `index_swing_horizontal` suite isn't on this branch. Its map uses the same `app::posting (index_swing)` spelling, so it will be selected the same way.

Effort: low
Changelog: none

Fixes #1021

## Process

title: fix(build): keep Cargo.lock intact in web/build-app-wasm.sh
body:
## What changed

`web/build-app-wasm.sh`: the `--config patch.crates-io...` build makes cargo rewrite the workspace `Cargo.lock` (flecs_ecs 0.2.2 / flecs_ecs_sys 0.2.1 lose `source` and `checksum`). The script now saves the tracked lock to `target/wasm-tools/Cargo.lock.keep` before its first cargo call (moved up from step 3, so `cargo fetch` and the wasm-bindgen install are covered too), and an `EXIT` trap restores it on success, failure and Ctrl-C/TERM. The header documents this; the only gap is SIGKILL, where the header says to run `git checkout -- Cargo.lock`.

Note: the main-branch script already had a restore trap on the cargo build step. The bug as filed reproduces only without it (a direct cargo call with the same `--config` dirties `Cargo.lock`). This PR moves the save/trap ahead of every cargo call and documents it.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/949-wasm-script-lock.md` (restore-from-copy chosen over a temp manifest dir).

## Readings (run in the worktree, `git status --short`)

- Before the change, direct cargo with the same `--config` patches: ` M Cargo.lock` (bug reproduced).
- Failed run, new script (wasm32 target not installed, so cargo fails after resolving): exit 101, `error[E0463]: can't find crate for core`; `git status --short` shows only the script edit, `Cargo.lock` clean.
- Interrupt check with the same save/restore shape and a 30 s step: lock dirty mid-run (` M Cargo.lock`), clean after SIGINT (EXIT trap runs on signal exit).
- `bash -n web/build-app-wasm.sh`: ok.

## Not exercised

- A successful full wasm build: the wasm32-unknown-unknown target is not installed on the test machine, so the success path was not run. It uses the same EXIT trap, but this is unverified by a real success run.
- No test was added. The repo has no shell-test harness, and a grep-style "script contains the trap" test would prove little. The readings above are the proof.
- No PowerShell twin exists (`web/` has only `build-app-wasm.sh`), so nothing to fix there.

## Notes

- `web/` scripts may be marked `needs-maintainer` by the PR reviewer as scripts; that is expected.
- Not a process file (not in AGENTS.md's list), so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump.
- Fork synced at v0.17.0.

Fixes #949
